newsitem.title: UK: U.S. fears hit Euro-shares but boost dollar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fears hit Euro-shares but boost dollar.

text.p: Fears the United States might raise interest rates to stem inflationary pressures dominated European financial markets on Friday, sending the dollar rising but sideswiping share markets.
A 160 point plunge in the Dow Jones Industrials Average overnight hit investor sentiment in Europe and stock markets across the continent opened with sharp falls.
The dollar in contrast benefited from the rekindled speculation over a U.S. rate rise although it later slipped back from its peaks against the mark and yen.
After the initial stocks reaction, shares crept off their lows, too, and some analysts questioned fears of a major bloodletting.
Dealers in London, Europe's biggest stock market, said activity was likely to be subdued ahead of the weekend and U.S. producer price data scheduled for 1330 GMT.
"People used the opportunity to bank some profits this morning, but we recovered because market makers want to keep fairly flat books and not get caught short of stock," said one senior trader.

Thursday's retail sales and weekly jobless claims data sparked the Dow's fifth steepest fall in point terms by underlining a growing likelihood that the Federal Reserve will act to tighten rates after its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25.

New York analysts cited a stiff bond market sell-off as the primary catalyst for the decline in stocks. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury fell nearly a full point to drive the yield up to 6.96 percent, its highest level in nearly six months.
That was reflected in Europe where British government gilts and German bund futures posted early losses.
Among Europe's big three bourses, Paris suffered the worst. The blue chip CAC-40 index was showing a decline of 1.3 percent by 1215 GMT but it had recovered from its lows.
Paris traders said the bourse was partly sustained by expectations that higher U.S. rates would push up the dollar and one broker said the selling pressure was limited.
"We've been falling for three days now," he said, adding that there appeared to be strong support at 2,595 points. "That seems to be holding."
Shares in Assurances Generales de France fell 5.22 percent to 203.3 francs, the biggest fall in the CAC index, after the group expressed interest in bidding for privatisation target GAN.
The German market, which was the worst performer of the big three on Thursday, followed the trend but recovered its losses late in floor trading with traders saying they were under no real pressure.
The bourse was drawing some support from the renewed strength of the dollar and buying interest remained alive on the domestic side.
The DAX-30 index of leading shares was down 0.38 points at 3,349 by 1215 GMT.
Shares in engineering group Mannesmann AG eased from their lows after the company issued a statement saying its earnings from ordinary activities would improve in 1997.
The shares earlier came under selling pressure as dealers said a well-respected investment research house had downgraded the stock but were still down 18.5 marks at 633.5.

British shares halved their opening losses as investors kept their nerve. The FTSE 100 index was 26 points, or 0.6 percent, lower at 4,371 by mid-session with declining stocks outnumbering gainers four to one.
Traders said domestic factors were helping to support the London market and the U.S. bond market had staged a moderate recovery.

"The UK is flush with cash," said Corey Miller, strategist at CL Laing. "There's a possibility of more special dividends...returning cash to institutions, and with interest rate expectations being reined back in the UK, people should still be looking to put that money back in the UK market."
Although the dollar made immediate gains after Thursday's U.S. data, it edged back during the European morning from its highs of 1.7100 marks and 123.85 yen.

"The retail sales report was yet another catalyst to point out to people that the same fundamental dollar-bull story is as valid now as it was a month ago," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7053 marks and 123.76 yen, compared Thursday's late European levels of 1.7030 marks and 122.92 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 26.3 points, or 0.6 percent, at 4,371.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 34.08 points, or 1.29 percent, at 2,598.02.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 0.38 points at 3,349.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $353.00 up 10 cents, while silver was up three cents at $5.29.
